doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: No bands from the plantations below Magnolia; Jim Humphrey teaching there
summary: Asked about Magnolia plantation, home of Chris Kelly and Jim Robinson, Martin says no bands came from there but Jim Humphrey went down to teach and Governor Warmoth hired a professor. A barber who played baritone came from there.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the band from down at the Magnolia plantation, where um... Chris Kelly came from up and down there. Jim Robinson was down there. Sonny Henry and...

They didn't have no bands come from down there. You didn't hear any musicians from down there. They didn't, the old man uh... See they were down there on the plantation. Deer Range. Deer Range. Yeah. And you take uh... You take old man... Uh... Ulfrey. Used to go down to teach him. Yeah, Jim Humphrey used to go down to teach him. Used to go down to teach him. Used to go down to teach him. Yeah. The man used to... Hire that professor that was Governor Warman. He was on Governor Warman plantation. Yeah.
For most of them they had a hall at Deer Range. Cause I played that one Sunday at Deer Range.

Yeah, but I'm speaking about... Way before that, you understand? And uh... Willie Parker and all them... Living down there? This man what I'm talking about uh... Used to live... Had that barber shop there, 1515 Biondler Street. Well now you take old man... Governor Warman, he had the professor going down there to teach him. Yeah. He was going to go down to Grand Olive. Yeah.
Well that barber, was he a musician too out of... You mentioned 15... 15 years ago. Yeah, yeah.
I forget him. He used to play... Baratone. Baratone. Baratone. He used to play a little... Brass band. He come from Barley, did he?
Hmm? He come from Barley, didn't he?
He come from down there... Down the river there... From Magnolia. Hmm.
